 THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 09.07.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 Bail Appl. No.5466 of 2025  2025:KER:50960  -3-  BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, J.
Dated this the 9th day of July, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioners are accused Nos.2 and 9 in Crime No.259 of 2023 of Paravur Police Station, Kollam,
registered for the offences punishable under sections 403, 405, 409, 418 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') and Sections 68(1), 32(c), 94(8) and 94(8)(A) of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (for short 'the Act').

3. According to the prosecution, pursuant to the report of the statutory audit under the Act, the accused, who are the Secretary, President and the Director Board members of the Kalakkode Service Co-operative Bank, was found to have committed various offences by fabricating forged documents and, in violation of the bye-laws, disbursed loans to persons on the basis of the same security and also disbursed other loans after showing a reduced value for the property and thereby caused a loss of Rs.2,26,51,694/- to the bank and committed the offences alleged.
Sri.V Venugopalan Nair, the learned counsel for the petitioner, contended that the prosecution allegations are false, and the petitioners have no role in the crime.

It was also submitted that, except S.Subhash vs State Of Kerala on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40099113/
2

sentences.text: the petitioners, all other Director Board members as well as the Secretary of the Society has been granted anticipatory bail and, therefore, petitioner should also be given a similar treatment.

The learned counsel further submitted that, pursuant to the interim direction of this Court on 02.05.2025, petitioners had appeared and have even co-operated with the investigation and, hence,
custodial interrogation is not necessary.
5.

Sri.Noushad K A, the learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the allegations are serious as the petitioners along with other accused are alleged to have caused huge loss to the bank.

The learned Prosecutor further pointed out that from the statutory auditors report, it was revealed that on the basis of a single security, three different persons were granted loans which were not legally permissible and the value of the single security was not sufficient to cover all the loans.

It was also pointed out that, another loan was granted, based on the security of 36 cents of paddy land,
showing not only an inflated value but also a value of Rs.2 Crores for a future building that was expected to be constructed, which has never been constructed till date.

According to the learned Prosecutor, despite the objections raised by the Secretary pointing 2025:KER:50960 out that there was no construction on the security offered, the loan was sanctioned, and the report indicates that till date no repayment has also been raised.
6. I have considered the rival contentions.
7. The Director Board members are arrayed as accused 3 to 17 and the President is the second accused while the Secretary of the Society is the first accused.
Accused Nos.3 to 17 except the nineth accused have already been granted anticipatory bail.

The petitioners were directed to appear before the Investigating Officer as per an interim order dated 02.05.2025 and the Investigating Officer was directed to inform whether further custodial interrogation is required.

8. The learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions from the Investigating Officer submitted that though the petitioners appeared pursuant to the interim order, further custodial interrogation is necessary in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.

9. Since all the other Director Board members have already been granted anticipatory bail on conditions and the petitioners were also directed to appear for interrogation, I am of the view that a parity has to be maintained amongst the accused, in the absence of any specific distinction that could be noted.

10. In Ashok Kumar v. Union Territory of Chandigarh, 2025:KER:50960 [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

On a consideration of the circumstances arising in the case, this Court is of the view that though the S.Subhash vs State Of Kerala on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40099113/
3 allegations are serious in nature, custodial interrogation of the petitioners are not required and petitioners are entitled to be released on pre-arrest bail on conditions.
Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 17.07.2025 from 10.00 am to 5.00 pm and again, if needed, on 18.07.2025 from 10.00 am to 5.00 pm., and shall subject themselves to interrogation.

sentences.text:
(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioners,
then, they shall be released on bail on them executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioners shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall they tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioners shall not commit any similar offences while they are on bail.
(f) Petitioners shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
